dictations.preRound: Admitted last night with cough and fever. Chest X-ray shows a right lower lobe opacity, possible pneumonia. Started ceftriaxone and azithromycin. SpO2 92% on 3 liters nasal cannula. No chest pain. If he needs more than 6 liters, call the ICU.
dictations.encounter: Still coughing, some rust-colored sputum. Crackles at the right base. Sputum culture and blood cultures pending. Continue current antibiotics and wean oxygen as tolerated.

note:
Subjective

The patient reports ongoing cough with rust-colored sputum.

Objective

Vital Signs: SpO2 92% on 3 liters nasal cannula.

Physical Examination: Crackles noted at the right base. No chest pain.

Testing Results

Chest X-ray: right lower lobe opacity, concerning for pneumonia.

Sputum culture and blood cultures pending.

Assessment

Patient is a 74-year-old male admitted with cough and fever, now with right lower lobe opacity on chest X-ray concerning for pneumonia. He is receiving intravenous antibiotics with clinical findings of crackles at the right base and productive cough with rust-colored sputum. Cultures are pending. Oxygenation is adequate at 92% on 3 liters nasal cannula. The clinical picture is consistent with community-acquired pneumonia; management will continue with current antibiotic therapy and oxygen support with escalation to ICU if oxygen requirement exceeds 6 liters.

Plan

1. Continue intravenous ceftriaxone and azithromycin for community-acquired pneumonia.
2. Wean oxygen as tolerated; escalate to ICU if oxygen requirement exceeds 6 liters.
3. Monitor sputum and blood culture results; adjust antibiotics based on culture sensitivities as available.
